detailed_section_hierarchy.full_explanation: Work measures energy transfer. Mechanical energy is conservative under gravity: KE + PE = Constant.

glossary_and_key_terms.definition: SI unit of work and energy, defined as work done by 1 Newton moving an object by 1 meter.

formulas_rules_and_laws.name: Work Done by Constant Force
formulas_rules_and_laws.variable_definitions: W=Work (J), F=Force in direction of motion (N), s=displacement (m)
formulas_rules_and_laws.model_application_example: Pushing 10 N object by 5 m = 50 J.

formulas_rules_and_laws.name: Kinetic Energy
formulas_rules_and_laws.model_application_example: 2 kg ball at 3 m/s has E_k = 0.5*2*9 = 9 J.

m3_practical_activities_lab_and_step_by_.activity_or_procedure_title: Investigating Energy Transformation with a Simple Pendulum
m3_practical_activities_lab_and_step_by_.objective_or_aim: Demonstrate interconversion of PE and KE.
step_by_step_procedure: Displace bob to extreme position A (PE maximum).
Release bob to swing to mean position B.
Observe swing to opposite extreme position C.
m3_practical_activities_lab_and_step_by_.expected_observations_or_working: Bob moves fastest at mean position B (KE max, PE min).
m3_practical_activities_lab_and_step_by_.scientific_or_logical_conclusion: Total mechanical energy E = KE + PE is conserved.

scripted_dialogues.speech_text: How much work is done by a porter carrying a 20 kg suitcase on his head while walking along a horizontal platform?

scripted_dialogues.speaker: Student
scripted_dialogues.speech_text: Zero work against gravity! The vertical force of gravity is perpendicular (90 degrees) to the horizontal displacement, so W = F * s * cos(90°) = 0.
